Dwight Dumais.b:
Former collegiate All-American diver and decorated international coach Dwight Dumais joined the Arizona coaching staff in August of 2018. He enters his ninth season leading the Wildcats diving efforts in 2026–27.
Leading Arizona's diving program, Dumais has seen immense success, guiding multiple divers to NCAA Finals, major conference achievements, and international acclaim.
Following a successful 2025–26 campaign, Dumais was named the Big 12 Men's Diving Coach of the Year. Dumais' men's diving squad placed in the top three at every event in every dual meet during the season. At Big 12 Championships, the men's team placed top three in every event and earned conference titles in the 1-Meter and Platform events. The culmination of the season's hard work was paid off with three men's divers qualifying for NCAA Championships, marking the first time the Wildcats had achieved the feat since 2001.
Dumais' also steered the development of Luke Hernandez in 2025–26, ending with Hernandez being named the Big 12 Men's Freshman of the Year. Hernandez claimed the Big 12 championship i nthe 3-Meter and finished second in the 1-Meter and Platform events en route to qualifying for NCAA Championships in all three.
In the 2024-25 season, Arizona’s diving squad saw immense in-season and postseason success under his leadership. There was not a single dual meet over the course of the season where an Arizona diver did not place in the top two in an event, and only one dual meet where an Arizona diver was not first in at least one event.
Dumais developed a well-rounded men's diving squad, composed of two freshman, as demonstrated in the squad’s second-place finish in the team diving event at the 2025 Big 12 Championships. Also at conference championships, all Arizona divers advanced to at least one final, and freshman diver Colin Agor was named Big 12 Freshman Diver of the meet. Additionally, Gage DuBois advanced to the “A” Final of every competition event he participated in. On the women's side, Brooke Earley and Zara Ayazi both advanced to two “A” finals, earning 54 points and 74 points, respectively, towards Arizona’s second-place finish at Big 12s.
This pattern of excellence was repeated and depth of Arizona’s diving squad with Dumais at the helm was demonstrated at the NCAA DI Zone E Diving Championships, where Earley, Ayazi and DuBois qualified for NCAAs. At NCAAs, DuBois was one of two male Arizona athletes to earn All-America Second Team honors in an individual event. Earley was the only Arizona athlete to make individual finals in an event at women’s NCAAs, advancing to finals in both the events she had qualified for (1m and 3m). Under Dumais’ direction, Earley was the second-highest finishing Big 12 diver in the NCAA 1m and 3m finals.
Among his many accomplishments at Arizona is the recruitment and development of Delaney Schnell, who would go on to become the most decorated diver in program history. Schnell finished her Arizona career with an NCAA Championship in Platform Diving, six Pac-12 diving championships, school records in the 3-Meter and Platform events, seven CSCAA All-America selections, and many more achievements. Schnell would go on to represent Team USA at both the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, where she earned a silver medal in 10-Meter Synchro, and the 2024 Paris Olympics.
Dumais, a five-time All-American diver at Stanford, was a coach at the internationally-renowned Longhorn Aquatic club at the University of Texas from 2010-2018 prior to joining the Arizona staff.
Dumais has served as a coach for USA Diving in various international competitions, including the 2017 World Championships in Budapest. His tutelage also includes one World Championship selection (2017), one World Cup selection (2018), one Junior World Champion (2016), one U.S. Olympic Trial finalist (2016), six Junior National Champions (2011, 2013, 2016, 2017) and nine senior national titles (2012, 2016, 2017, 2018).
The Ventura, California native was a five-time All-American diver at Stanford, where he won the 2007 and 2009 one-meter Pac-10 Championship and was named 2006 Pac-10 Newcomer of the Year.
In addition to international coaching experience, Dumais was also a decorated diver on the international stage, with experience from the junior level through the senior level. Dumais was a six-year member of the USA Diving team (2009, 2011-15) and qualified for the Olympic Trials in 2012 and 2016. Dumais won the Senior National Synchronized Three-Meter Championship in 2012.

Jay Holmes.b:
Jay Holmes was hired by Head Coach Been Loorz to join the Arizona Swim & Dive program on Aug. 6, 2025.
Holmes joined the Wildcats following 40 years coaching at Texas A&M, including 21 years as the head coach of the Aggies men's swimming and diving program from 2004-24.
"We are excited to welcome Coach Holmes and his wife Annette to the Wildcat Family," Loorz said at the time of his hiring. "Jay has been a beacon of professionalism and character in the NCAA for a long time. I know the staff will benefit from his experience, and the athletes from his ability to connect."
Across the final four years of Holmes' tenure at Texas A&M the men's program broke every single one of the program's records. In total, during his illustrious coaching career, Holmes has developed nine Olympians, 77 All-Americans, one CSCAA Swimmer of the Year, and two conference Swimmers of the Year. Following the 2004–05 season he was named the Big 12 Men's Coach of the Year on the back of the Aggies second place conference and 15th place NCAA finish.
"I am very grateful to Coach Loorz, his staff, and the University of Arizona for this opportunity," Holmes said at the time of his hiring. "Arizona Swimming & Diving has a great history and great tradition. Being part of that is a privilege I am excited about. Taking time away form coaching last year allowed me to experience a lot of life that I would not have been able to do otherwise. As much as I enjoyed that time, it's time to get back at it. My wife and I look forward to arriving in Tucson and starting our adventure as Wildcats!"
Prior to his head coaching stint at Texas A&M, Holmes spent 19 years as an assistant coach with the Aggies. He served as an assistant coach for the men's and women's programs from 1986–1995 and moved over to exclusively develop the men's program from 1995–2004.
Holmes swam four years with the Aggies from 1980–84 and graduated from the university with a bachelor of science degree in Business Administration in 1984.
Holmes and his wife, Annette, have two children: Meredith Joy and Cooper Samuel.

Amanda Beard.b:
Legendary Wildcat, seven-time Olympic medalist, and NCAA Champion swimmer Amanda Beard was hired as an assistant coach by head coach Augie Busch on June 20, 2023.
Beard, arguably one of the most accomplished athletes in Arizona Athletics history, returned to her alma mater where she was enshrined into the Hall of Fame in 2008.
Beard's work, as both a coach and an athlete, has brought the program immense success.
In the 2024-25 season, Beard helped lead Arizona Swim & Dive to multiple finals finishes at both the Big 12 Championships and D1 NCAA Championships. Beard also assisted in overseeing the women's first conference relay gold and conference individual gold since 2013 and the women's team's highest conference finish (2nd) since 2008.
Over the course of her second season as a member of the Arizona coaching staff, Beard guided the Cats to 16 top-ten program record-setting performances in addition to 80% of Arizona's active roster earning at least one personal best.
"This is incredibly exciting and significant for Arizona Swimming & Diving," Busch said at the time of her hiring. "Amanda's legendary athletic career speaks for itself. She is one of the all-time great Wildcats and an all-time great in the sport. I believe she has equal potential in teaching and coaching at this level. We are blessed and thrilled to have her back in Tucson."
During her time as a Wildcat, Beard hauled in an NCAA National Championship in the 200 meter breaststroke, 10 All-America selections, and helped lead a breakthrough 2000 Arizona Women's team to their first ever Pac-10 Championship, among many other accomplishments.
"I am extremely grateful for the opportunity to join the University of Arizona Swimming & Diving family," Beard said at the time of her hiring. "It is an honor to be invited back into a program that was home to me and helped me during a very important part of my career. I know the dedication and hard work it takes to achieve success in the pool and I am excited to share my knowledge with the swimmers at Arizona."
Beard, a California native, broke onto the scene at the 1996 Atlanta Olympic Games where she brought home a gold medal in the 400 meter medley relay and a pair of silver medals in the 200 and 100 meter breaststroke events.
In the years following that breakout performance in Atlanta, Beard established herself as one of the most accomplished women's athletes in the breaststroke in the sport's history. The remainder of her swimming resume includes four more Olympic medals, three World Championships medals, four Short Course Worlds medals, and a pair of Swimming World American Swimmer of the Year awards in 2003 and 2004.
When it was all said and done in the pool, Beard was inducted into the International Swimming Hall of Fame in 2018.
Beard also brings with her to Tucson over 20 years of coaching experience, highlighted by a pair of seasons as a volunteer coach at UCLA, seven years as a technical stroke coach at Beard Swim Co., and three years as a stroke consultant at King Aquatics.
In 2010 Beard co-founded and has since served as the Chief Operation Officer of Beard Swim Co., one of the nation's premier swim schools, in Washington.
Beard is joined in Tucson by her husband Sacha Brown, son Blaise, and daughter Doone.

Caitlin DeNise.b:
Caitlin DeNise was hired by Head Coach Ben Loorz in July 2026 to serve as an Assistant Coach with the Wildcats.
DeNise came to Tucson following five seasons at Lewis & Clark College — she began her tenure with the River Otters as an assistant coach for two years before moving into an interim head coaching role for the 2023-24 season and eventually earning the full-time head coach position for the 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons.
"We are excited to welcome Caitlin and her husband Wes to the Wildcat family," Loorz said at the time of her hiring. "Coach DeNise is a veteran coach with a great breadth and depth of experience. From the college to club level, assistant coach to head coach, she brings a great base of knowledge and a proven track record of treating athletes well."
While at Lewis & Clark, DeNise developed 31 all-conference student-athletes and guided the River Otters to 13 program records and over 60 top 10 times in program history. As the Lewis & Clark head coach, DeNise steered the men's side to 370 points at the 2024-25 Northwest Conference Championship, their most since 1998, and the women's side to 217 points at the 2025-26 NWC Championship, their most in six years.
"I look forward to joining Arizona Swimming and Diving, a program with a championship tradition and momentum building around it," DeNise said at the time of her hiring. "I would like to thank Coach Loorz for trusting me with this opportunity. I am excited to work together with this incredible group of student-athletes and coaches to bring championships to Tucson."
DeNise's experience also includes time as an assistant coach at Cal State Easy Bay from 2018–21, a senior assistant coach with the Pleasanton Seahawks from 2016–18, and an assistant coach at University of the Pacific from 2015–16.
Prior to her coaching career, DeNise swam collegiately at Cal State East Bay where she qualified for the NCAA DII Finals in the 100 butterfly and earned the school's Female Athlete of the Year award. Her program records in the 100 butterfly (54.78) and the 100 butterfly (54.78) at Cal State East Bay still stand to this day.
DeNise is joined in Tucson by her husband, Wes.

Ben Loorz.b:
Ben Loorz was hired as the head coach of Arizona Swimming and Diving by Vice President and Director of Athletics Desireé Reed-Francois on May 15, 2024. He enters his third season leading the Wildcats in 2026–27.
Coach Loorz, the 2025–26 Big 12 Women's Swimming Coach of the Year, has overseen the development of 65 All-Big 12 performers and 21 CSCAA All-Americans across two seasons at Arizona. Loorz joined the Wildcats after eight seasons of championship success as the head coach at UNLV.
## With the Wildcats
The Wildcats continued their climb in their second season with Loorz at the helm, finishing second at the Big 12 Men's and Women's Championships, capturing six Big 12 Conference Championships, and sending 19 qualifiers to NCAA Championships (11 men, 8 women). Arizona's successes led to Loorz being named the 2025–26 Big 12 Women's Swimming Coach of the Year.
Arizona's 2025–26 season concluded with both teams ranked in the CSCAA Top 25, with the men checking in at No. 17 and the women ranked at No. 24. Across the course of the season, the Wildcats set three program records and posted 19 swims that landed among the top 10 fastest times in program history.
Of the 19 NCAA Championship qualifiers that the Wildcats sent to Atlanta, highlights included Tomas Lukminas posting a program record 41.11 in the 100 Free to finish seventh, and the women's 200 Free Relay finishing inside the top 10.
In his first season at Arizona in 2024–25, Loorz oversaw a men's program that ended the season in the top 25 nationally, and men's and women's teams that set multiple school records, earned multiple All-American and all-conference honors, and finished second in the Big 12 Conference.
Arizona men’s swimming roster ended the year with seven All-Big 12 First Team Honorees and four Second Team Honorees, in addition to five CSCAA All-American Second Team Honorees. Additionally, Coach Loorz led the Wildcats to their highest conference championship finish since 2020, with the program’s first conference relay championship gold in the 200 freestyle relay. Under the direction of Coach Loorz, seven male Arizona swimmers qualified for the NCAA Championships, and Arizona’s qualifying 400 freestyle relay set a program record and finished 12th in the nation (2:47.64).
On the women's side, under Loorz's direction, the Cats earned their highest finish at a conference championship (2nd) since 2008. Nine Wildcat swimmers were awarded All-Big 12 First Team Honors, three earned All-Big 12 Second Team Honors and four Arizona swimmers were named to the CSCAA All-America Second Team after impressive performances at the NCAA Championships. Also at the Big 12 Championships, Arizona's women secured the program’s first conference relay gold and conference individual gold since 2013. During his first season as the head coach of the program, four Wildcat women set top-ten program times, and over 80% of the active Wildcat roster swam personal bests in at least one event.
During Coach Loorz’s first year in Tucson, four new school records were set (400 free relay-2:47.64, 100-yard freestyle-41.56, 800 freestyle relay: 6:10.62, 200 freestyle-1:31.48), 16 top-ten program times were posted, and more than 80% of Arizona’s active roster earned a personal best in at least one event.
"We sought to hire a head coach with a successful record of coaching, recruiting and holistically developing student-athletes at the highest of levels," Reed-Francois said at the time of his hiring. "Coach Loorz is a proven leader who is nationally recognized in the swimming and diving community with a championship vision for our program. He is a tireless recruiter with an exceptional history of developing championship culture and will grow upon the legacy of the program as we enter the Big 12 Conference. We are proud to welcome Coach Loorz, his wife Jenn, and their family to the University of Arizona."
## Before Arizona
Loorz guided UNLV to a WAC conference crown in men's swimming in his final season, marking the Rebels fourth consecutive conference championship while setting a conference record in scoring. He was also named the WAC Swimming Coach of the Year for a fourth straight year in 2024. UNLV's women's program, which competes in the Mountain West, tied a school record with 15 all-conference performers in 2023-24 while Vika Yanovska won the 1-meter dive crown last season to give UNLV its first ever MW diving title. Loorz was also named the 2021 MW Women's Swimming Coach of the Year.
Throughout his eight seasons in Las Vegas, Loorz coached the Rebels to a total of five WAC and MW conference championships while earning five runner-up finishes. The program has set nearly 40 school records during his tenure in addition to winning 70 WAC and 20 MW individual and relay championships.
"I want to thank the search committee, Desireé Reed-Francois, University leadership and the entire Arizona Athletics Department for the opportunity to continue the storied legacy of this program while growing and developing our student-athletes to become champions," Loorz said at the time of his hiring. "The University of Arizona is a special place, and my family and I can't wait to get to campus and begin this exciting journey together."
UNLV student-athletes have amassed numerous conference honors under Loorz's leadership, which include Ruby Howell being named the MW Freshman Swimmer of the Year in 2021, George Ratiu earning WAC Freshman Swimmer of the Year in 2021 and Kris Matuszewski repeating the feat in 2023. The Rebels also had a pair of representatives, Zsuzsanna Jakabos and Vuk Celic, compete at the 2021 Tokyo Olympic Games. Loorz also trained Kasia Wasick, from Poland, who finished fifth in the 50-meter freestyle in the Tokyo Games before becoming the top sprinter in the world in 2022 and 2023.

Peter Richardson.b:
Former Arizona staff member Peter Richardson, who helped guide the Wildcats distance swimmers from 2019–22, was hired to return to Tucson as an associate head coach for Arizona Swimming & Diving by head coach Ben Loorz on June 13, 2024.
In his first season back at Arizona, Richardson oversaw a successful Arizona program that finished runner-up on both the men's and women's sides at Big 12 Championships and sent multiple athletes to NCAAs.
Under Richardson's guidance, 25 Arizona athletes were Big 12 finalists, leading the Cats to runner-up finishes for both the men and women. At these same conference championships, 17 Arizona athletes made the All-Big 12 first team and eight were awarded second team honors.
Also during Richardson's first year back with the Cats, 16 Arizona athletes qualified for the NCAA Championships, 11 of whom were named to the CSCAA All-American Second Team. Richardson also guided an Arizona program that saw four records broken and 16 top-ten times set during the 2024-25 season.
Upon his hiring of Richardson, head coach Ben Loorz commended Richardson's energy, passion and capabilites as a coach and recruiter, qualities which he demonstrated throughout this first season back.
"I'd like to welcome coach Richardson back to the Wildcat family! His passion for the University of Arizona, and for the student-athletes, always shines through," Loorz said at the time of his hiring. "He's a world-class recruiter and a high-integrity coach. I know the swimmers are going to love his energy and will immediately benefit from his vast experience and knowledge."
Following three years in Tucson, Richardson logged a successful two-year stint in Los Angeles with the USC Trojans. During the 2023-24 season under Richardson's guidance the USC women achieved a runner-up finish at the Pac-12 Championships and placed eighth at the NCAA Championships. The Trojan women's perfect 9-0 record in dual meet competition last year was their first undefeated mark in program history. Richardson's mark extended internationally at USC as well, as he oversaw the training of four Olympic A-cut qualifiers while with the Trojans; all four will compete in the 2024 Paris Olympics.
"Coach Loorz does things the right way and we have always talked about teaming up. I could not be more excited to return to this special place," Richardson said at the time of his hiring. "Arizona is one of only six men's and seven women's teams who have won an NCAA Team Championship since 2000 — this is a place we can win. Arizona has world-class facilities, world-class tradition, and we're going to make sure to recruit and develop in that same fashion!"
In August of 2023, Richardson was the head coach for Team USA at the World University Games in Chengdu, China. There he led Team USA to 33 finals and seven medals, representing nearly one third of all Team USA medals won. Richardson's guidance helped steer Keaton Jones to a gold medal in the 200 back, the only gold medal won by the entire Team USA delegation.
During his first tenure with the Wildcats, coach Richardson helped fuel three successful campaigns for the Arizona distance swimmers, highlighted by a pair of Pac-12 Championships by Brooks Fail in the 1650 free event.
The Wildcats distance group picked up three NCAA A-cuts and nine B-cuts under Richardson's guidance during the 2021–22 season. The year prior, during the 2020–21 season, Richardson helped Fail accomplish one of the best individual NCAA Championship performances in program history; Fail placed third in the 500 free, fourth in the 1650 free, and eighth in the 200 fly. Fail's career-best time of 14:31.38 in the 1650 free broke a 22-year-old school record and his 4:09.41 mark in the 500 free went down as the 13th fastest time by a man in world history.
Richardson achieved success immediately at Arizona during the 2019–20 season, his first with the Wildcats. The Arizona men finished second at the Pac-12 Championships, tied for the highest finish in program history. The Wildcats distance crew qualified four individuals for the NCAA Championships that year.
Prior to his first stop in Tucson, Richardson spent seven seasons as the head coach at the University of the Pacific. During his time with the Tigers an incredible 73 school records were established and in 2018 the program was one of just two programs in the nation to achieve an NCAA A-cut relay time without a full allotment of scholarships.
He began his coaching career at Fresno Pacific University, where as the head swimming coach he led the men's side to back-to-back NAIA National Championships in 2010 and 2011, along with a women's NAIA National Championship in 2012.
Richardson swam collegiately at the University of the Pacific, where as a team captain he helped the Tigers seal back-to-back Big West Championships in his junior and senior campaigns.
Richardson is joined in Tucson by his wife, Jonelle, and his four children Gabrielle, Brooklynn, Peter, and Juliette.
## Richardson's Arizona History
## 2021-22 Season
In his third year as Associate Head Coach, Richardson coached Senior Brooks Fail to another PAC 12 Championship in the 1650 freestyle. At the NCAA Championships, Brooks Fail earned All-American honors in 500 freestyle (5th), 400 IM (6th) and 1650 freestyle (7th). Fail’s success in the pool led him to be one of only 8 athletes in the NCAA to score in all three “A” Finals in back-to-back years. Additionally, Brooks broke Arizona’s school record in the 400 IM (3:38.55). Arizona’s freshmen distance swimmers had big drops at the PAC 12 Championships – Elizabeth Mackowiak (4:55 – 4:48), Stella Copeland (4:54-4:49) and Beck Parnham (4:27-4:21) in the 500 freestyle. Sophomore Tia Lindsay dropped ten seconds in her 400 IM, going 4:16.93 at the PAC 12 Championships. All in all, the Arizona distance group picked up three NCAA “A” Cuts and nine “B” Cuts during the season.
